P1.evidence: Three-part frame only — 'go into what you're... what trying to achieve, where we're currently at, see if we can actually help you with that... If I feel like this is just not the best fit... I'll point you in the right direction' — no 'what you need' element. Frame agreement taken ('How does that sound?' → 'Yeah. Perfect. So take me through it'). Open question run verbatim in substance: 'what are you specifically trying to achieve with working on your fitness and mobility?' No setter notes exist to read back.

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight all collected ('How old are you, if I may ask?' → 45; 5'4"; 'I'm 215'). Diet covered properly. But work was never asked — the job loss surfaced only because she volunteered it. No question at all about health conditions, injuries, pain, sleep or energy from a 45-year-old at 215 lb who mentioned doctors talking to her about bone loss.

P3.evidence: Ran the surface layer well — 'is there any other goals outside of physically... Maybe getting your confidence up, mobility, longevity?' and 'why is it important for you to focus on it right now? Is there something that happens in your life recently'. Then stopped. She handed him bereavement, job loss and 'get my life back' and he did not go one level deeper into who else it affects, identity or legacy.

P4.evidence: 'Have you already tried to change that before and it may be failed?' → 'I've done it before but not as consistent... then life will hit me again'. She named the gap herself: 'Sounds like you want more one-on-one guidance and support.' Never asked the root-cause question about why she cannot stick to it on her own.

P5.evidence: No two-year consequence frame, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not'. The closest move was 'Do you feel like it is for you the right time at the moment to actually take a different approach' — a timing check, not a line in the sand. The rep did probe 'what if life hits you again in a couple of months?' but dropped it when the audio broke up.

P6.evidence: 'do you feel like there's something that would stop you? Maybe family or something else in your life' was run twice and pushed on. But the belief question ('do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure') was never asked, and the rep declared fit — 'it sounds like it's a good fit' — without a clean commitment yes.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted; the call was rescheduled before any presentation.

objection_plays.detail: Prospect disclosed having paid thousands of dollars to online programmes that abandoned her — a provider-trust objection. There is no scripted play for it. The rep validated the feeling and pivoted to 'you want more one-on-one guidance', but offered no proof, no reference, no differentiation of what makes this different. She was left holding the same doubt.

notes: Baseline is the weak phase: no health, injury, sleep or energy questions on a 45-year-old at 215 lb. The rep ended the call for audio reasons, which was defensible, but he told her it was 'a good fit' before running consequence or commitment — that verdict was not earned by the discovery he actually did.
